title: Maximum of Minimum Values in All Subarrays
summary: Given an integer array nums, compute the maximum of the minimum values for all subarrays of sizes ranging from 1 to the length of nums.
statement: Given an integer array nums, compute the maximum of the minimum values for all subarrays of sizes ranging from 1 to the length of nums. For each size i, find the minimum value in all subarrays of size i+1, then determine the maximum of these minimum values. Return an array where each element represents the result of these queries.
constraints: nums has 1 through 100000 values from 0 through 1000000000.
For every window size 1..n, return the largest among all window minimums.
Output index width-1 corresponds to that window width.

def maximum_of_window_minimums(nums):
    size = len(nums)
    left = [-1] * size
    stack = []
    for index, value in enumerate(nums):
        while stack and nums[stack[-1]] >= value:
            stack.pop()
        left[index] = stack[-1] if stack else -1
        stack.append(index)
    right = [size] * size
    stack = []
    for index in range(size - 1, -1, -1):
        while stack and nums[stack[-1]] > nums[index]:
            stack.pop()
        right[index] = stack[-1] if stack else size
        stack.append(index)
    answer = [-1] * size
    for index, value in enumerate(nums):
        width = right[index] - left[index] - 1
        answer[width - 1] = max(answer[width - 1], value)
    for index in range(size - 2, -1, -1):
        answer[index] = answer[index + 1]
    return answer

hints: Each value is the minimum of the widest interval bounded by the nearest strictly smaller value on each side.
Use monotonic stacks for those boundaries, place each value at its maximum supported width, then propagate answers from larger widths downward.
Find left smaller and right smaller-or-equal; update answer[width-1]; scan backward taking max with answer[next].

Every window minimum supports its window width, and its maximal span records that support. Any value valid for a larger width is also attainable for every smaller width, justifying backward propagation.
